title: Every moment plants seeds
hook: each moment brings seeds of life that mostly go unnoticed

segments.voice: Yesterday, the false self and the true self: the image, and the self God knows. Your line was who god sees. Today, Merton on what lands in an ordinary day.

Dandelions don't ask permission. One puff of wind and their seeds are everywhere: in the cracks of the sidewalk, on the car windshield, in your hair. Plenty land where nothing can grow. A few catch. An ordinary day can work the same way. A stranger's kindness at the checkout. A line from a song. A friend's text at exactly the wrong moment, or the right one. Thomas Merton believed every one of those moments carries something God is planting. And most of it, he said, blows right past us.
screen: `DANDELIONS DON'T ASK PERMISSION.` → `A KINDNESS, A SONG, A TEXT.` → `MOST OF IT BLOWS PAST.`

segments.voice: First, the line. Near the start of New Seeds of Contemplation, the book from two days ago, Merton says that every moment and every event of every life plants something in the soul. Seeds of grace, blown in on the wind of ordinary days. Second, why they're missed. He says most of these seeds die because people aren't ready to receive them. Not because they're wicked. Because they're distracted, hurried, somewhere else. The seeds land on hard ground. Third, the Gospel picture. Merton didn't invent this image. Jesus tells of a sower who throws seed everywhere: on the path, on rocks, among thorns, and on good soil. In Luke, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus explains it simply: "The seed is the word of God." The sower is almost careless with it. He doesn't check whether the ground is ready. He just keeps throwing. It fits Merton's idea: grace thrown into every moment, whether anyone's paying attention or not. Fourth, the good soil. In another parable, in Mark, Jesus says the seed grows while the farmer sleeps, and he doesn't know how. You don't make the seed grow. Your part is smaller: be the kind of ground where it can land. That's where waking up comes back. An awake heart catches more seeds. And one caught moment, a sentence, a face, a small mercy, can grow for years.
screen: `EVERY MOMENT PLANTS SOMETHING.` · `MOST SEEDS LAND ON HARD GROUND.` · `THE SOWER THROWS EVERYWHERE.` · `BE GROUND WHERE IT CAN LAND.` · then, large: `THE SEED IS THE WORD OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Go back through today so far, slowly, like rewinding a video, and find one small thing that landed: a word someone said, a moment of beauty, a nudge to call someone, a feeling you brushed away. Don't judge whether it was important; just hold it for a minute, like a seed in your hands. If you pray, you can ask for it to grow.
Sower, Jesus's image of grace thrown into every moment, careless whether the ground is ready. Today's word.
Your line: seeds everywhere. Even on the most ordinary day, something is landing. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Catholics end the day with a short examen, looking back over the day for moments of grace and giving thanks, a practice that goes back to Saint Ignatius of Loyola.
